MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How many factors does 36 have? (1 mark)
   A. 10
   B. 8
   C. 11
   D. 9

2. Round 765 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 760
   B. 700
   C. 780
   D. 770

3. Which number is written in words as "eight thousand, two hundred and six"? (1 mark)
   A. 8,206
   B. 82,006
   C. 8,026
   D. 826

4. Which of these shows 270 in words? (1 mark)
   A. two hundred and seventy
   B. three hundred and seventy
   C. twenty-seven
   D. two hundred and seven

5. Work out 6,478 + 2,355. (1 mark)
   A. 8,833
   B. 8,843
   C. 8,733
   D. 8,723

6. What is 63 × 30? (1 mark)
   A. 189
   B. 93
   C. 18,900
   D. 1,890

7. What is 96 ÷ 3? (1 mark)
   A. 33
   B. 42
   C. 31
   D. 32

8. What is 63 ÷ 3? (1 mark)
   A. 21
   B. 20
   C. 22
   D. 31

9. In 56 ÷ 8 = 7, the number 8 is called the (1 mark)
   A. dividend
   B. remainder
   C. divisor
   D. quotient

10. In the fraction 2/3, what does the numerator 2 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How many of the equal parts are taken
   B. The number of wholes
   C. How many equal parts the whole has
   D. The size of each part in centimetres

11. A circle is cut into 10 equal parts and 7 parts are shaded. What fraction is not shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 3/10
   B. 3/7
   C. 7/10
   D. 10/3

12. In the fraction 5/8, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 8
   C. 13
   D. 3

13. In the fraction 4/12, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 12
   C. 4
   D. 16

14. In the number 13.42, the digit 2 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tens
   B. Ones
   C. Hundredths
   D. Tenths

15. Which is greater, 0.5 or 0.45? (1 mark)
   A. They are equal
   B. It cannot be told
   C. 0.45
   D. 0.5

16. In the number 4.05, the digit 5 is in which place? (1 mark)
   A. Tens
   B. Hundredths
   C. Tenths
   D. Ones

17. What is 75 cm in metres? (1 mark)
   A. 0.075 m
   B. 75 m
   C. 7.5 m
   D. 0.75 m

18. A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its perimeter? (1 mark)
   A. 28 cm
   B. 13 cm
   C. 40 cm
   D. 26 cm

19. A rectangle is made of 12 rows with 7 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 84 square units
   B. 38 square units
   C. 19 square units
   D. 96 square units

20. Cuboid A is 5 by 2 by 4 blocks (length, width, height). Cuboid B is 4 by 4 by 2 blocks. Which has the greater volume? (1 mark)
   A. Cuboid B
   B. Cuboid A
   C. It cannot be told
   D. They are equal

21. A cuboid has a volume of 60 blocks. One layer has 12 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 48
   C. 5
   D. 72

22. A basket of mangoes has a mass of 8 kg. The empty basket has a mass of 1 1/2 kg. What is the mass of the mangoes? (1 mark)
   A. 6 kg
   B. 6 1/2 kg
   C. 7 kg
   D. 9 1/2 kg

23. What is 2 1/2 kg + 3/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 kg
   B. 3 1/2 kg
   C. 3 1/4 kg
   D. 3 kg

24. A bus leaves at 7:45 a.m. and the journey takes 2 hours 30 minutes. At what time does it arrive? (1 mark)
   A. 10:15 a.m.
   B. 9:15 a.m.
   C. 9:75 a.m.
   D. 10:45 a.m.

25. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 6 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 6. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 6:30
   B. 6:45
   C. 6:06
   D. 7:30

26. How long is a lesson that starts at 1:15 p.m. and ends at 4:50 p.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 20 min
   B. 3 h 35 min
   C. 3 h 45 min
   D. 4 h 35 min

27. A shopping list has three items costing Ksh 3,200, Ksh 4,100 and Ksh 1,550. What is the total cost? (1 mark)
   A. Ksh 8,750
   B. Ksh 8,860
   C. Ksh 8,850
   D. Ksh 8,950

28. Kip faces West and makes a half turn. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. East
   C. South
   D. North

29. An angle that is smaller than a right angle looks like (1 mark)
   A. a corner that is more closed than a square corner
   B. a straight line
   C. a circle
   D. a corner that is more open than a square corner

30. The table shows the favourite fruits of 10 pupils: mango 4, banana 3, orange 2, pawpaw 1. What is the total of all the numbers? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 9
   C. 11
   D. 10

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Write the next three numbers in the pattern 2,000, 2,300, 2,600, 2,900. (3 marks)

32. How many right angles does a rectangle have? Explain. (2 marks)

33. A lesson starts at 8:15 a.m. and ends at 10:40 a.m. How long is the lesson? (3 marks)

34. A trader sold goods worth Ksh 3,568 on Monday and Ksh 2,276 on Tuesday. (a) Find the total. (b) Estimate the total by rounding each amount to the nearest ten. (c) How far is the estimate from the exact total? (5 marks)

35. Amina has a 3 L jug of water. She pours 1 1/4 L into a pot and 1/2 L into a cup. How much water is left in the jug? (4 marks)

36. Work out 34 × 100 and 60 × 100. (2 marks)

37. Amina says the area of a rectangle with 4 rows and 6 columns is 10 because 4 + 6 = 10. Explain her mistake and give the correct area. (3 marks)

38. At what times on a clock do the hands make a right angle and a straight line? Give one example of each. (4 marks)

39. Find the first common multiple of 4 and 6 by writing the first six multiples of each number. (4 marks)

40. For the number 4,835: (a) write it in expanded form, (b) give the total value of the digit 8, (c) round it to the nearest ten, (d) say whether it is even or odd. (5 marks)

41. Find and name three objects in the classroom that show a rectangle, a circle and a triangle. (3 marks)

42. Change 45/100, 6/100 and 7/10 into decimals. (3 marks)

43. Explain what a right angle is. State how many right angles there are in (a) a rectangle, (b) a straight line, (c) a full turn. (5 marks)

44. Fill in the 3 times table from 3 × 1 to 3 × 10. Describe one pattern you notice. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #16 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 9
   The factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. There are 9 of them.

2. D — 770
   Look at the ones digit 5. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 765 rounds to 770.

3. A — 8,206
   eight thousand, two hundred and six: put each part in its place and use 0 where there is no digit. The number is 8,206.

4. A — two hundred and seventy
   270 = two hundred and seventy. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

5. A — 8,833
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 6,478 + 2,355 = 8,833.

6. D — 1,890
   63 × 3 = 189, then × 10 gives 1,890.

7. D — 32
   3 × 32 = 96, so 96 ÷ 3 = 32.

8. A — 21
   3 × 21 = 63, so 63 ÷ 3 = 21.

9. C — divisor
   The number we divide by is the divisor. 56 is the dividend and 7 is the quotient.

10. A — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 2/3 it says that 2 parts are taken.

11. A — 3/10
   Not shaded: 10 − 7 = 3 parts, so 3/10.

12. B — 8
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

13. B — 12
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

14. C — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 13.42 the digit 2 is in the hundredths place.

15. D — 0.5
   Compare the tenths first. 0.5 is greater than 0.45.

16. B — Hundredths
   The first digit after the decimal point is tenths and the second is hundredths. In 4.05 the digit 5 is in the hundredths place.

17. D — 0.75 m
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: 75 cm in metres is 0.75 m.

18. D — 26 cm
   Perimeter = 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 26 cm.

19. A — 84 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 12 × 7 = 84 square units.

20. B — Cuboid A
   A = 5 × 2 × 4 = 40 blocks. B = 4 × 4 × 2 = 32 blocks. Cuboid A is greater.

21. C — 5
   Layers = 60 ÷ 12 = 5.

22. B — 6 1/2 kg
   8 − 1 1/2 = 6 1/2 kg.

23. C — 3 1/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 2 1/2 kg + 3/4 kg = 3 1/4 kg.

24. A — 10:15 a.m.
   7:45 + 2 hours = 9:45. 9:45 + 30 minutes = 10:15 a.m.

25. A — 6:30
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 6 shows 6 × 5 = 30 minutes, so the time is 6:30.

26. B — 3 h 35 min
   Count on from 1:15 p.m. to 4:50 p.m.. The total is 3 h 35 min.

27. C — Ksh 8,850
   Add the three costs: 3,200 + 4,100 + 1,550 = 8,850.

28. B — East
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. West followed by a half turn gives East.

29. A — a corner that is more closed than a square corner
   Its arms are closer together than the arms of a right angle.

30. D — 10
   Add all the numbers: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3,200, 3,500, 3,800 (rule: add 300)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rule and 2 marks for the three correct numbers.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: 4. A rectangle has four corners and each corner is a right angle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 4 and 1 mark for the reason.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 25 minutes
   Working / marking points: 8:15 to 10:15 is 2 hours (1 mark); 10:15 to 10:40 is 25 minutes (1 mark); total 2 h 25 min (1 mark).

34. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) Ksh 5,844 (b) 3,570 + 2,280 = Ksh 5,850 (c) 6 shillings more than the exact total
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the exact total with regrouping, 1 mark for both rounded numbers, 1 mark for the estimate 5,850, 1 mark for the difference 5,850 − 5,844 = 6.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: 1 1/4 L
   Working / marking points: 1 1/4 + 1/2 = 1 3/4 L used (2 marks); 3 − 1 3/4 = 1 1/4 L (2 marks).

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3,400 and 6,000
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each. Move each digit two places left.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: She added the rows and columns. Area is rows × columns = 4 × 6 = 24 square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying she added, 1 mark for saying multiply, 1 mark for 24.

38. (4 marks)
   Answer: Right angle: 3 o'clock (or 9 o'clock). Straight line: 6 o'clock.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for a right angle example and reason, 2 marks for a straight line example and reason.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24. Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. The first common multiple is 12.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct list and 2 marks for identifying 12.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) 4,000 + 800 + 30 + 5 (b) 800 (c) 4,840 (d) odd because it ends in 5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part; part (a) needs all four addends, part (b) 8 × 100, part (c) the ones digit 5 rounds up, part (d) needs the reason from the ones digit (1 mark for the classification plus reason together).

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example a blackboard (rectangle), a clock face (circle) and a set square (triangle).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct object matched to a shape.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.45, 0.06 and 0.7
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct decimal.

43. (5 marks)
   Answer: A right angle is a square corner, made by a quarter turn. (a) 4 (b) 2 (c) 4
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for explaining a right angle (square corner or quarter turn), 1 mark for each of (a) 4, (b) 2 and (c) 4.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30. Each product is 3 more than the one before it (or the products alternate odd and even).
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for the table (1 mark if one or two errors), 2 marks for a correct pattern with a reason.
